thread:
tina.support: FYI customer reported duplicate side-effects + billing for one user action. They say the client got a 202 Accepted then retried and ended up with two 'send_payment' calls. Attached small log snippet from their app (redacted request ids).
julian.sre: Ugh. 202 + client retry pattern can definitely cause duplicate execs if we return early and the SDK retries. Do we have the raw request/response headers + correlation-id from the gateway? Need to know if our response had an idempotency header or not.
mike.eng: Posting quick snippet of what they'd sent (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-infer-1",
  "input": "Charge $12.50 to user 0xabc",
  "function_call": {
    "name": "send_payment",
    "arguments": {"user_id":"0xabc","amount_cents":1250}
  }
}
```
mike.eng: They didn't include an idempotency_key field. Our gateway currently only honors idempotency if client supplies one in `x-idempotency-key` header. If client retries after 202 we can see double execs.
sarah.ops: Customer timestamped two billing events 3s apart: 2026-03-10T12:31:45Z and 2026-03-10T12:31:48Z. Billing shows two unit events for function execution. I've opened a billing hold but we should triage root cause before refund.
dev-bot: Canary deploy "idempotency-guard-v1" rolled out to 10% at 1865123000, health ok. This patch rejects duplicate function calls within 5s when request contains `x-idempotency-key` or a matching request fingerprint.
julian.sre: Two immediate asks:
1) @tina.support — can you ask the customer for the full raw response they received (headers + body) at the first 202? We need to know if we sent any `Retry-After` or `x-request-id`.
2) @mike.eng — can you try to repro locally by sending identical request twice without idempotency header and see if send_payment is called twice? If yes, capture gateway logs.

mike.eng: Will repro now. Quick repro curl I used:

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d @payload.json \
 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Send it twice in quick succession, or simulate network drop so client retries.

julian.sre: If we confirm gateway returned 202 with empty body, that's likely the cause. We should consider returning a small idempotency token in body or require `x-idempotency-key` for endpoints that trigger non-idempotent tools.

billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-8932 for the two events; hold applied to duplicate charge. Customer notified that we are investigating. (ref: invoice #INV-3344)

mike.eng: Repro steps succeed on staging: send_payment executed twice when no idempotency header. Adding `x-idempotency-key` deduplicates correctly. Logs: `tool.invoke send_payment -- exec_id=abc123` twice when no header.

julian.sre: Good repro. Short-term mitigation: tell support to ask affected customers to retry with idempotency header and we've issued a manual refund for the duplicate charge (billing already started hold). Medium-term: implement server-side fingerprinting when function args are identical and request timestamps < 10s.

tina.support: Noted. I'll reply to customer w/ ask for raw response and recommend retry with `x-idempotency-key`. Also confirming billing took action.

mike.eng: I'll open PR to return `x-server-request-id` in response body on 202s and add a warning in docs about idempotency for function-calling endpoints.

julian.sre: Assigning follow-ups: mike -> implement server token in 202 + docs, eng -> server-side short-window dedupe RFC, support -> collect raw response + confirm refund, billing -> finalize charge reversal. Marking P1 for customer impact.

tina.support: Thanks all. I'll update thread when customer responds. :thumbsup:
